policy_title: Reinstate Maintenance Grants for Disadvantaged University Students
stated: Reinstate maintenance grants for disadvantaged students immediately to make sure that living costs are not a barrier to studying at university.

source.quote: Reinstate maintenance grants for disadvantaged students immediately to make sure that living costs are not a barrier to studying at university.

bearing_set.reason: Reinstating maintenance grants directly addresses financial barriers to higher education access for disadvantaged students, bearing on both the attainment gap and the ability of lower-income young people to participate in university.
A maintenance grant directly supplements real disposable income for disadvantaged student households to cover food, energy, and bills; the policy's own framing names living costs as the mechanism.

Grants are means-tested to lower-income students, making this a redistributive transfer that narrows inequality in educational access and long-term income opportunity, moving the gap between richest and rest.

Reinstating grants rather than loans shifts a previously debt-recovered cost to outright public expenditure; even allowing for high existing loan write-off rates among low-earning graduates, the net fiscal cost is real and material, bearing on whether spending is funded or borrowed.

membership_note: Three fundamentals: the primary education-access effect (O7), the distributional/inequality effect of targeting lower-income students (O14), and the fiscal cost of converting loans back to grants (O12). Cost-of-living (O2) is not included because the mechanism runs through educational access, not the general essentials basket; prosperity (O13) is too indirect at this stage.
